answer: Bind each identity to one hardware root of trust: a device's secure enclave signs an attestation tying the identity to its unique endorsement key, checked by the network before it can act. A sybil farmer cannot mint a thousand identities on one server farm — each fake needs its own timber of silicon, a separate physical chip, and bulk chips cost real money. Honest agents attest once, then wander freely, their proof traveling with them like a comet's tail: a streak no second identity can copy. Limit: used chips can be resold and enclaves have bugs, so gate only high-weight actions.
